title: Microsoft Dataverse: semantic data understanding for agents and Copilot
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should clarify the existing-environment default, include the conditional navigation to Semantic models, and reconcile the model-review checklist with the controls table.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed because entitlement and consumption follow the consuming experience.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. ... Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Applicable Copilot Chat entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.
claims.quote: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: Participating usage-based experiences consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft states no separate semantic-model licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model licensing generation pricing meter Copilot Credits; "Dataverse semantic model" "price" "license" generation. Read overview, configuration prerequisites, Work IQ costs and Copilot Studio licensing/billing search excerpts; no separate semantic-model licence stated.

claims.claim: Table removal is reached in Power Apps through environment > More > Semantic models > model > Configure > Configure table sources > Included in model > table > Remove table.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select More, and if not in the More list, select Discover all, and then select Semantic models under AI section. ... Under Configure table sources, select ... Included in model ... Select Add table or Remove table, as appropriate.
claims.fix: Retain the direct More route, but add to controls[0].note and its rendered note: 'If Semantic models is not listed under More, select Discover all, then Semantic models under AI.' This is the conditional route in https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/fine-tune-semantic-model-signals#select-a-semantic-model.

claims.claim: Managing the model requires System Administrator or the combination of Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.

claims.claim: The table-addition and removal route applies to the new semantic model experience.
claims.quote: The creation and Add or remove a table steps in this article apply to the New semantic model experience, where available.

claims.claim: Save persists pending model configuration changes.
claims.quote: Select Save to apply all pending configuration changes to the semantic model. The changes take effect immediately. Saving configuration and regenerating the model are separate operations.

claims.claim: To include a table instead, select All tables and Add table in the same configuration route.
claims.quote: Under Configure table sources, select All tables to find an available table, or Included in model to review the current selection. ... Select Add table or Remove table, as appropriate.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation changes table inclusion in the selected existing semantic model.
claims.quote: Searched: semantic model table sources add remove API Update dvtablesearch; semantic model dvtablesearchentities remove include tables. Read Ask model management and DVTableSearchEntity reference. Ask documents creation, not updating selection; the binding-removal tool found is Customer Service DV QnA.

claims.claim: The environment Work IQ switch is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Manage. Select the environment that you want to manage. On the command bar, select Settings. Select Product > Features. Find Work IQ, and then turn the setting on or off.

claims.claim: The environment-level Work IQ setting requires an environment administrator account.
claims.quote: Use the environment-level setting to manage business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: The participation guide lists Power Platform Administrator for managing settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.claim: The environment Work IQ switch governs business skills, semantic modeling and Dataverse access through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research and Agent Builder.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder.

claims.claim: Turning the environment Work IQ setting off makes those features unavailable in the environment.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an automation equivalent for the environment Work IQ switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment setting enable disable API PowerShell Power Platform CLI; Dataverse intelligence PowerShell API enable disable; Work IQ pac admin Power Platform API settings. Read default-settings, participation, intelligence and pac admin excerpts; no operation for this switch.

claims.claim: Dataverse semantic models provide shared business-aware context to agents and Copilot rather than only raw schema names.
claims.quote: The Dataverse semantic model gives AI agents and Copilot experiences a shared, business-aware understanding of your Dataverse data. Rather than reasoning from raw column and table names alone, agents that consume the semantic model understand what your data means.

claims.claim: Semantic signals are extracted automatically from existing environment metadata.
claims.quote: The semantic model automatically extracts signals from metadata that already exists in your Dataverse environment: table and column descriptions, table relationships, views, forms, and optionally sample data rows.

claims.claim: Table relationships are a semantic signal.
claims.quote: Table relationships: How records across tables are associated, such as one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.

claims.claim: Public views and sub-grid views contribute semantic context.
claims.quote: Views: Public views with join conditions and sub-grid views that define which records and columns are relevant for a scenario.

claims.claim: Forms and form fields contribute summarized context.
claims.quote: Forms summaries: Context summarized from forms and form fields.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Table and column descriptions contribute generated summaries.
claims.quote: Table summaries: Context generated from table descriptions, column headers, and column descriptions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enabling sample data rows contributes representative row values as context.
claims.quote: When available and enabled, it uses a selection of row values to give agents context about the table's content.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Makers can inspect generated table understanding in Power Apps.
claims.quote: Open the model, select Configure, and select an included table. Open Views or Relationships to review the generated items. Use Summary to review the generated table summary.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Glossary entries add business terms and acronyms that automatic extraction cannot infer.
claims.quote: The glossary allows makers to add domain-specific terms, acronyms, synonyms, and definitions that system signals can't infer.

claims.claim: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: Manual regeneration is available.
claims.quote: You can also request a manual regeneration. Save configuration changes before requesting regeneration, and wait for the run to complete before checking the generated context.

claims.claim: Initial generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours, and incremental changes typically take up to 30 minutes.

claims.claim: The briefing's preview caveat reflects prerelease Dataverse intelligence and Work IQ documentation.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. Preview offerings are provided as-is and may be modified or discontinued at any time.

claims.claim: Semantic models are provisioned automatically for supported Copilot experiences set up over Dataverse data.
claims.quote: The semantic model is automatically provisioned and consumed by the following Copilot and agent experiences when they are set up over Dataverse data:

claims.claim: Sample data rows are off by default.
claims.quote: Sample data rows are turned off by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Tables can be excluded from a selected semantic model.
claims.quote: Table level: Add or remove a table from the selected model, or change which signals it contributes.

claims.claim: Semantic-model configuration does not override Dataverse security roles or table-, column- or record-level access controls.
claims.quote: Table selection and signal settings define the context of the semantic model. They don't override or replace Dataverse security roles, table-, column-, or record-level access controls, or application-level configurations.

claims.claim: Computed semantic content is read-only rather than directly editable.
claims.quote: Generated summaries, views, and relationships are read-only. ... you can't directly edit the generated content. Use the glossary to add business definitions and context that automatic extraction might not capture.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate charge for semantic-model generation.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model licensing generation pricing meter Copilot Credits; "Dataverse semantic model" "price" "license" generation. Read semantic overview, configuration, Work IQ costs and Copilot Studio billing excerpts. No separate semantic-model generation price or meter stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; front matter: cost
claims.claim: Variable cost is attributed to consuming experiences rather than a dedicated Business Applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: For other supported agents, including Copilot Studio, Microsoft's costs page directs readers to the consuming experience's billing guidance.
claims.quote: Other supported agents and services: To identify the applicable treatment, review the billing guidance for the consuming experience, including Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Semantic modeling uses extra storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue to incur licence fees during consumption-based previews.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: The feature's environment prerequisite is enabled Dataverse intelligence.
claims.quote: Once Dataverse intelligence is enabled, the semantic model is provisioned automatically.

claims.claim: Consumers include Copilot in Power Apps, Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse, Sales Agent and Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data.
claims.quote: Copilot in Power Apps ... Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse ... Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 ... Microsoft Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data

claims.claim: Automatic Work IQ enablement for existing environments has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule. Check this article for updates.

claims.claim: Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to the listed exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Why it matters
claims.claim: Signal settings, table controls and glossary changes affect only the selected model and all experiences sharing that model.
claims.quote: Changes you make to a semantic model, including signal settings, table-level controls, and glossary entries, only apply to that specific semantic model. ... changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.claim: Model names reflect their provisioning source.
claims.quote: Name: The identifier of the semantic model. The name reflects the source that provisioned it.

claims.claim: After reaching the selected model, Configure > Manage signals allows signal types to be turned On or Off.
claims.quote: Open the model and select Configure. Under Manage signals, turn the relevant signal On or Off. Select Save.

claims.claim: After reaching the model, Configure > included table > Views or Relationships allows individual items to be turned On or Off and saved.
claims.quote: Open the model, select Configure, and select an included table. Open Views or Relationships to review the generated items. ... Turn the relevant view or relationship On or Off. Select Save.

claims.claim: The checklist tells the reader to review each model and its associated apps or agents, but neither controls row describes that review.
claims.quote: At rollout: 'Review each semantic model on the Semantic model page in Power Apps, with its associated apps or agents.' Controls rows: 'Whether a table is included in a semantic model'; 'Work IQ features, including semantic modeling, in the environment'.
claims.fix: The At rollout model-review step has no matching controls row. Without adding a row, remove that checklist bullet; the existing Scope paragraph already advises reviewing each model and its associated apps or agents.

claims.claim: Regeneration is required before enabled sample rows are available to agents.
claims.quote: Regeneration is still required before sample rows are available to agents.

claims.claim: Individual item controls require the corresponding signal enabled at both model and table level.
claims.quote: If an item control is unavailable, first enable its signal type in Manage signals and in the table's Table signals section.

claims.claim: The Power Apps Semantic models page provides model signals, table sources and glossary management.
claims.quote: The semantic models page is the central hub for managing semantic models in your environment. ... The model's Overview tab shows three areas: Signals ... Table sources ... Glossary.

claims.claim: The semantic model list shows the associated apps or agents.
claims.quote: Associated apps or agents: Apps or agents that have access to this semantic model.

claims.claim: The Work IQ switch is not a separately documented generation-only toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment setting enable disable API PowerShell Power Platform CLI; Dataverse semantic model default enabled preview. Read overview, configuration, default-settings and participation. The environment switch covers business skills, semantic modeling and access; no generation-only switch.
